hook_text: Yellow, violet, brown. In five seconds you will know that means 470 ohms, and why.
clip_script: Ten colours, ten digits: black brown red orange yellow green blue violet grey white, 0 to 9. Hold the lone gold band to the right. First band, a digit. Second band, a digit. Third band, how many zeros. Yellow violet brown: 4, 7, one zero, 470 ohms. That is the resistor that saves your LED. Red red red: 2200. Brown black orange: 10 000. Gold at the end means within 5 percent, which for an LED is plenty. Unsure? Multimeter on ohms, resistor loose, not in your fingers. And on the diagram write the number, never the colours.
visual_style: Whiteboard colour strip 0 to 9; a resistor with four bands and arrows labelling digit, digit, zeros, tolerance; 4 7 0 appearing beneath; a multimeter reading 468.
mood: Brisk and satisfying, like cracking a code.
pacing: Colours, hold it, digit, digit, zeros, 470, two more, gold, meter, write the number.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and read every resistor in your kit before checking with a meter.
